zhSummary: 它为大多数工作相关伤害和职业病提供法定福利；通常不以谁有过错为前提。
enSummary: A statutory benefit system for most work injuries and occupational diseases; fault is generally not the starting test.
enTitle: What is workers’ compensation?
historicAnswer: Workers’ compensation is a system of benefits provided by law to most employees who experience work-related injuries or occupational diseases.  Generally, benefits are paid regardless of fault.

zhSummary: 委员会中立地处理争议，能解释程序，却不能替任何一方提供法律意见。
enSummary: The Commission resolves disputes as a neutral agency. Its staff can explain procedure, but cannot advocate or give legal advice.
enTitle: What is the Illinois Workers’ Compensation Commission?
historicAnswer: The Illinois Workers’ Compensation Commission is the State agency that administers the judicial process that resolves disputed workers’ compensation claims between employees and employers. The Commission acts as an administrative court system for these claims. As the administrative court system, the Commission must be impartial.  Staff explains procedures and basic provisions of the law to members of the public, but cannot provide legal advice or act as an advocate for either the employee or employer.

zhSummary: 在伊利诺伊州受雇、受伤或工作关系主要位于本州的多数员工，从开始工作起可能受保护。
enSummary: Most employees hired or injured in Illinois, or whose employment is localized there, are covered from the start of work.
enTitle: Which employees are covered by the Workers’ Compensation Act?
historicAnswer: Most employees who are hired, injured, or whose employment is localized in the State of Illinois are covered by the Act.  These employees are covered from the moment they begin their jobs.

zhSummary: 关键是伤病是否在工作过程中发生并与工作有关；职业病同样可能符合。
enSummary: The injury must arise out of and occur in the course of employment; qualifying occupational disease can also be covered.
enTitle: What injuries and diseases are covered under the law?
historicAnswer: The Workers’ Compensation Act provides that accidents that arise out of and in the course of employment are eligible to receive workers’ compensation benefits.  This generally means that the Act covers injuries that result in whole or in part from the employee’s work.

zhSummary: 医疗、临时全残、临时部分失能、职业康复与生活维持、永久部分失能、永久全残、遗属福利。
enSummary: The handbook groups benefits into medical care, TTD, TPD, rehabilitation and maintenance, PPD, PTD, and survivor benefits.
enTitle: What benefits are provided?
historicAnswer: The Act provides the following benefit categories, which are explained in later sections of this handbook: a) Medical care that is reasonably required to cure or relieve the employee of the effects of the injury; b) Temporary total disability (TTD) benefits while the employee is off work, recovering from the injury; c) For injuries that occur on or after February 1, 2006, temporary partial disability (TPD) benefits while the employee is recovering from the injury but working on light duty  for less compensation; d) Vocational rehabilitation/maintenance benefits are provided to an injured employee who is participating in an approved vocational rehabilitation program; e) Permanent partial disability (PPD) benefits for an employee who sustains some permanent disability or disfigurement, but can work; f) Permanent total disability (PTD) benefits for an employee who is rendered permanently unable to work; g) Death benefits for surviving family members. 4

zhSummary: 手册说明工伤赔偿福利通常不计入州或联邦所得税收入。
enSummary: The handbook says workers’ compensation benefits generally are not taxable income under state or federal law.
enTitle: Are workers’ compensation benefits taxable income?
historicAnswer: No.  Workers’ compensation benefits are not taxable under state or federal law and need not be reported as income on tax returns.

zhSummary: 雇主承担法定义务，可由保险公司支付，也可获准自保；不能把保费或福利成本转嫁给员工。
enSummary: The employer is responsible, often through insurance or approved self-insurance, and cannot charge the employee for the premium or benefit.
enTitle: Who pays for workers’ compensation benefits?
historicAnswer: By law, the employer is responsible for the cost of workers’ compensation benefits.  Most employers buy workers’ compensation insurance, and the insurance company pays the  benefits on the employer’s behalf.  No part of the workers’ compensation insurance premium or benefit can be charged to the employee.  Other employers obtain the state’s approval to self-insure, which means that the employer will be responsible for paying its own claims. To identify the party responsible for paying benefits, an employee may check the employer’s workplace notice, check the Commission’s website, or contact the Commission at inscompquestions.wcc@illinois.gov  or toll-free at 866/352-3033.

zhSummary: 维持保险或自保、张贴通知、保存与上报事故记录，并不得因员工行使权利而报复。
enSummary: Employers must secure coverage, post the notice, keep and report injury records, and avoid retaliation.
enTitle: What does the law require of employers?
historicAnswer: Employers are obligated to follow the provisions of the Workers’ Compensation Act.  Employers must: a) purchase workers’ compensation insurance or obtain permission to self-insure from the Commission; b) post a notice in the workplace.  Employers can obtain this notice at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/forms.htm; and c) keep records of work-related injuries and report to the Commission those accidents involving more than three lost workdays. Employers are prohibited from doing the following: a)  charging  the employee for any part of the workers’ compensation insurance premium or benefits; and e) harass, discharge, refuse to rehire, or in any way discriminate against an employee for exercising his or her rights under the Workers’ Compensation Act.

zhSummary: 向 IWCC 的保险合规部门提供雇主信息和受伤日期；联系方式以现行官网为准。
enSummary: Report the employer and injury details to the IWCC Insurance Compliance Division; use current contact information.
enTitle: What should an employee do if his or her employer does not have workers' compensation insurance?
historicAnswer: The employee should give the employer's name and address, and the date of injury, to the Commission’s Insurance Compliance Division.  The Division can be reached at inscompquestions.wcc@illinois.gov or at 312/814-6611, toll-free 866/352-3033.

zhSummary: 雇主可能面临刑事与民事处罚、停工命令，并可能失去工伤法下的某些保护。
enSummary: An uninsured employer can face civil and criminal penalties, a stop-work order, and loss of certain Act protections.
enTitle: Is an employer subject to any penalties if they do not purchase workers’ compensation insurance?
historicAnswer: Yes. There are various provisions in the Workers’ Compensation Act that address this issue. Negligent failure to provide workers’ compensation insurance coverage is punishable by a Class A misdemeanor for each day without coverage (maximum 12 months imprisonment, $2,500 fine). Knowing failure to provide workers’ compensation insurance coverage is punishable by a Class 4 felony for each day without coverage (maximum 1-3 years imprisonment, $25,000 fine). An uninsured employer may also be subject to a civil penalty of $500 for every day it lacked insurance, with a minimum $10,000 fine. 5 Employers without workers’ compensation insurance may be subject to a citation issued by the Insurance Compliance Division.  The citation fine may range from $500 to $2,500. An uninsured employer loses the protections of the Workers’ Compensation Act for the period of noncompliance.  That means an employee who was injured during the period of noncompliance may choose to sue in civil court. In addition, if the Commission finds that an employer knowingly failed to provide insurance coverage, it may issue a stop-work order and shut the company down until it obtains insurance.

zhSummary: 蓄意虚报索赔、为拒付作假、或为未提供的医疗服务收费，都可能构成欺诈。
enSummary: Intentional false claims, false denials, and billing for services never provided can be fraud.
enTitle: Does the Workers’ Compensation Act address workers’ compensation fraud?
historicAnswer: Yes.  Workers’ compensation fraud falls into many different categories that affect employees, employers, and healthcare providers.  The Act prohibits the intentional filing of any fraudulent workers’ compensation claims or making a fraudulent statement to obtain workers’ compensation benefits.  Workers’ compensation fraud may also involve making false statements in order to deny workers’ compensation benefits.  It is also unlawful to intentionally present a bill or statement for the payment of medical services that were not provided. Assisting or conspiring in any of these actions may also be considered workers’ compensation fraud.

zhSummary: 处罚随涉案价值变化，也可能涉及返还款项、诉讼费用和律师费；具体数额应核对现行法律。
enSummary: Penalties vary with the value involved and can include restitution and costs; verify current statutory amounts.
enTitle: What are the penalties for workers’ compensation fraud?
historicAnswer: The penalties for violations of the fraud provisions increase with the value of the property obtained or attempted to be obtained, starting with a Class A Misdemeanor for property valued at $300 or less (maximum 12 months imprisonment and a $2,500 fine), and ranging upwards to a Class 1 felony (maximum 4-15 years imprisonment, $25,000 fine) for property valued at more than $100,000.  A convicted party is required to pay complete restitution, as well as court costs and attorney fees.

zhSummary: 向伊州保险部门举报真实疑虑；故意作虚假举报本身也有法律后果。
enSummary: Report a genuine concern to the Illinois Department of Insurance; knowingly false reports can themselves be penalized.
enTitle: What should I do if I suspect workers’ compensation fraud?
historicAnswer: If you wish to report a possibly fraudulent situation, contact the Workers’ Compensation Fraud Unit, Department of Insurance (DOI.WorkCompFraud@illinois.gov; toll-free 877/923-8648). Anyone who intentionally makes a false report of fraud is subject to a Class A misdemeanor (maximum 12 months imprisonment, $2,500 fine).

zhSummary: 尽快告知雇主，并保留可以证明通知时间与内容的记录。
enSummary: Tell the employer promptly and keep a record of when and what you reported.
enTitle: Who should an employee notify if injured at work?
historicAnswer: The employee should inform their employer if they are injured at work.

zhSummary: 尽可能说明事故的大致日期与地点；手册允许口头或书面通知。
enSummary: Include the approximate date and place if known; the handbook allows oral or written notice.
enTitle: Are there any specific requirements for a notice of an accident to an employer?
historicAnswer: The Act provides that the notice of accident shall include the approximate date and place of the accident, if known.  Notice may be given orally or in writing.

zhSummary: 普通事故通常最迟 45 天；放射暴露及职业病有不同触发点，须按具体事实核对。
enSummary: Most accidents have a 45-day notice limit; radiation exposure and occupational disease have different triggers.
enTitle: What are the time limits for notifying the employer of a workplace accident?
historicAnswer: Generally, the employee must notify the employer as soon as practicable, but no later than 45 days after the accident.  Any delay in the notice to the employer can delay the payment of benefits. For injuries resulting from radiological exposure, the employee must notify the employer 90 days after the employee knows or suspects that he or she has received an excessive dose of radiation. 6 For occupational diseases, the employee must notify the employer as soon as practicable after he or she becomes aware of the condition.

zhSummary: 应安排急救和医疗、通知承保方；停工超过三天时，支付 TTD 或书面说明缺少资料及拒付理由。
enSummary: The employer should arrange care, notify its carrier, and, after more than three days off, pay TTD or explain its information need or denial in writing.
enTitle: What should the employer do after receiving notice of accident?
historicAnswer: The employer should promptly take the following steps: a) provide all necessary first aid and medical services; b) inform the insurance carrier or workers’ compensation administrator, even if the employer disputes the employee’s claim; c) if the employee cannot work for more than three days because of the injury, the employer must do one of the following: (i) Begin payments of TTD; or (ii) Give the employee a written explanation of the additional information the employer needs before it will begin payments; or (iii) Give the employee a written explanation of why benefits are being denied.

zhSummary: 保存工作相关死亡、伤害与疾病的准确记录；单纯急救且无其他影响的轻微事件有例外。
enSummary: Keep accurate records of work-related deaths, injuries, and illnesses; minor first-aid-only events may be excluded.
enTitle: What records about workplace injuries must the employer maintain?
historicAnswer: Employers must maintain accurate records of work-related deaths, injuries, or illnesses.  This does not include minor injuries requiring only first aid and not involving further medical treatment, loss of consciousness, restriction of work or motion, or transfer to another job.

zhSummary: 死亡事故及导致超过三个预定工作日缺勤的伤病有 Form 45 报告义务，期限因类别而异。
enSummary: Form 45 reporting covers work deaths and injuries or illnesses causing more than three scheduled workdays lost, with different deadlines.
enTitle: Are employers required to submit any reports to the Commission?
historicAnswer: Yes.  Employers are required to report accidents to the Commission on the form, “Employer’s First Report of Injury” which is known as the Form 45.  The Form 45 is available on the Commission’s website, http://www.iwcc.il.gov/forms.htm. Written reports of all job-related deaths must be made to the Commission within two working days. Written reports of job-related injuries or illnesses resulting in the loss of more than three scheduled workdays must be made within one month.  Employers are not required to submit a Form 45 for injuries that do not result in three or less days of lost work.

zhSummary: 雇主按 IWCC 当前的电子报告渠道提交，而不是把事故报告当成员工索赔申请。
enSummary: Employers use the IWCC’s current electronic accident-reporting channel; this report is separate from an employee claim.
enTitle: How do employers submit accident reports?
historicAnswer: Accident reports should be submitted electronically.  For information on how to submit accident reports electronically, please visit the Commission’s website at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/forms.htm.

zhSummary: 雇主须张贴 IWCC 制定的工伤通知；请从现行官网获取版本。
enSummary: Employers must post the IWCC workplace notice; obtain the current form from the agency.
enTitle: Are employers required to post any notices in the workplace?
historicAnswer: Yes. Employers are required to post a notice developed by the Commission at each respective place of employment.  The Commission maintains a cop y of this notice on its website at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/forms.htm.

zhSummary: 先查明拒付原因，再考虑向 IWCC 正式立案；雇主的事故报告不会自动启动争议审理。
enSummary: Ask why payment stopped or was denied, then consider filing a claim. An employer accident report does not start a Commission case.
enTitle: What are an employee’s options if the employer refuses to pay for workers’ compensation benefits?
historicAnswer: The employee or the employee’s attorney should contact the employer directly to determine why benefits are not being paid.  Poor communication often causes delays and misunderstanding. If the employer still does not pay any benefits, the employee’s other option is to file a claim at the Commission.  Please note that an accident report does not trigger any action by  the Commission. 7 The Commission becomes involved only if the employee files a claim and follows the procedures to request a hearing.  For more information about the claims process at the Commission, please see the next section of the handbook.

zhSummary: 因行使工伤权利而遭报复违法，可能另行诉讼；雇主仍可基于独立的合法理由管理人事。
enSummary: Retaliation for exercising Act rights is prohibited, while discipline for separate valid reasons remains possible.
enTitle: Can an employee be fired for reporting an accident or filing a claim?
historicAnswer: It is illegal for an employer to harass, discharge, refuse to rehire, or discriminate in any way against an employee for exercising his or her rights under the law.  Such conduct by the employer may give rise to a right to file a separate suit for damages in the circuit court. An employee with a pending workers’ compensation claim may still be disciplined or fired for other valid reasons.

zhSummary: 2013 手册写的是纸质三份；现行 IWCC 使用 CompFile，律师和自行代理者须电子提交。
enSummary: The 2013 paper-copy instruction is obsolete. Current IWCC filing uses CompFile for attorneys and self-represented litigants.
enTitle: How is a claim filed at the Commission?
historicAnswer: To start your claim at the Commission, you must file three copies of the Application for Adjustment of Claim, along with a Proof of Service stating that a copy of the application was served upon the employer.  Claims may be filed by mail or in person at any Commission office.  You can find these forms on the Commission’s website at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/forms.htm.

zhSummary: IWCC 手册说明表格及立案没有收费。
enSummary: The IWCC handbook states that its forms and filing a claim carry no fee.
enTitle: Is there a filing fee for filing documents at the Commission?
historicAnswer: No.  There are no fees for the forms or to file a claim.

zhSummary: 2013 版旧网址已过时；使用 IWCC 现行表格页与 CompFile 指南。
enSummary: The 2013 forms URL is outdated; use the current IWCC forms page and CompFile guidance.
enTitle: Where are the required claim forms at the Commission posted?
historicAnswer: All forms are posted on the Commission’s website at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/forms.htm.  These forms are available in Microsoft Word and Adobe Acrobat format and can be filled in on a personal computer.

zhSummary: 案件获编号并分配仲裁员；双方要主动跟进状态日与审理请求，长期不推进可能被驳回。
enSummary: A case number and arbitrator are assigned; parties must track status calls and request hearings, or an inactive case may be dismissed.
enTitle: What happens after a claim is filed?
historicAnswer: The Commission assigns a case number and an arbitrator to the case.  For cases in Cook County, cases are randomly assigned among the Chicago arbitrators.  For cases outside of Cook County, cases are assigned to the hearing site closest to the site of the accident. Every three months, the case will automatically be set for a status call.  At the call, the parties may request a trial.  If neither party requests a trial, the case is continued for another three months. This rotation continues for three years.  For the first three years after a case is filed, it is the parties’ responsibility to move the case along.  After three years, the arbitrator may dismiss the case at the status call unless the parties show there is a good reason to continue it. It is important to realize that each arbitrator is responsible for thousands of cases, cannot monitor individual cases, and has no information as to whether benefits are or are not being paid.  It is the parties’ responsibility to track the case and take action when appropriate.

zhSummary: 通过现行 CompFile 门户查询案件信息，而非使用旧手册中的失效地址。
enSummary: Use the current CompFile portal for case information, not the 2013 legacy URL.
enTitle: How can I determine the status of a case at the Commission?
historicAnswer: The Commission maintains an online database of cases on its website.  You can search that database by name or case number at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/caseinfo.htm. 8

zhSummary: 雇主可自愿支付；要让 IWCC 命令支付、或保护未来争议中的权利，则需要考虑正式立案。
enSummary: Voluntary payments can occur without a case, but a Commission order requires a filed claim.
enTitle: Is an employee required to file a claim at the Commission in order to receive benefits?
historicAnswer: No.  However, many employees choose to file a claim.  If the employee wants the Commission to order benefits to be paid, he or she must file a claim.  An employee who is receiving benefits  but is concerned about protecting his or her rights to receive future benefits may also wish to file a claim.

zhSummary: 多数案件为受伤等事件后三年，或最近一次 TTD／医疗账单支付后两年，以较晚者为准；疾病等有例外。
enSummary: Most claims use the later of three years from injury, death, or occupational disablement, or two years from the last TTD or medical payment; exceptions exist.
enTitle: What are the time limits for filing a claim at the Commission?
historicAnswer: Generally, an employee who fails to file a claim within the time limits loses his or her right to claim future benefits. In most cases, the employee must file a claim within three years after an injury, death, or disablement from an occupational disease, or within two years of the last payment of TTD or a medical bill, whichever is later. Some cases involving specific diseases or death of an employee have different time limits.  You may wish to consult an attorney in those instances.

zhSummary: 员工接受福利不等于放弃其他权利；雇主先付款也不等于承认全部责任。
enSummary: Accepting voluntary benefits does not waive the worker’s rights, and payment does not waive the employer’s ability to dispute liability.
enTitle: Does the voluntary payment of benefits affect a claim?
historicAnswer: If the employee accepts benefits from their employer, he or she does not give up any rights under the law.  Similarly, if the employer pays benefits, it does not waive its right to dispute the claim.  Even if a claim is filed with the Commission after some benefits have been paid, the employer still has the right to contest its liability to pay any compensation at all.

zhSummary: 不强制；自行代理者要自己追踪案件、出庭并提出证据，中立的仲裁员不能代为辩护。
enSummary: Counsel is optional, but a self-represented person must manage the case and evidence; the arbitrator remains neutral.
enTitle: Does the employee have to hire an attorney to file a claim?
historicAnswer: No, but in disputed cases, most employees and employers do hire attorneys. If the employee does not hire an attorney, it is the employee’s responsibility to keep track of the claim, appear at hearings when necessary, and present evidence at hearings that proves his or her eligibility under the law. Arbitrators and commissioners must be neutral and are subject to the Code of Judicial Conduct . They cannot act as an advocate for the employee or for the employer. The Commission cannot recommend attorneys.  Employees seeking an attorney may wish to ask friends for a recommendation or call an attor ney referral service.  The Commission has a list of bar associations that make referrals at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/attys.pdf.

zhSummary: 手册说明一般有 20% 等限制，及时自愿支付的部分不能收费；协议须经委员会批准。
enSummary: Fees are regulated, generally with a 20% cap and no fee on timely voluntary payments; the representation agreement needs approval.
enTitle: How much can an attorney charge for their services on a workers’ compensation case?
historicAnswer: The law limits the claimant attorney’s fee: a) An attorney shall not charge any fee on payments the employer voluntarily made in a timely and proper manner for medical care, TTD, and any other compensation. b) The attorney's fee is limited to 20% of compensation recovered, up to 20% of 364 weeks of the maximum TTD benefit, unless a hearing is held and the Commission approves additional fees. c) If the employer made a written offer to the employee, the attorney may only charge a fee on the amount recovered in excess of this offer.  In this case, the attorney’s fee may exceed 20% of the additional amount recovered, but in no event may the fee exceed 20% of the total award. d) The attorney's fee must be stated on the Attorney Representation Agreement form, signed by the employee (or in death cases, by the beneficiaries) and approved by the Commission. 9

zhSummary: IWCC 不处理员工与自己律师之间的争执；应直接沟通并寻求独立法律帮助。
enSummary: The Commission does not resolve disputes between a claimant and their attorney; seek independent advice.
enTitle: What if the employee is dissatisfied with his or her attorney?
historicAnswer: The Commission cannot resolve problems between an injured employee and his or her attorney.

zhSummary: 要求 IWCC 命令支付的一方通常由员工证明自己符合条件。
enSummary: The employee bears the burden of proving entitlement to an award.
enTitle: What must the employee demonstrate to obtain an order from the Commission awarding benefits?
historicAnswer: In cases before the Commission, it is the employee’s responsibility to prove he or she is eligible for benefits.  The employer does not need to disprove an employee’s claim.  By law, the burden of proof rests with the employee.

zhSummary: 逐项看管辖、雇佣关系、工作事故或暴露、医学因果关系、及时通知；之后还可能争金额与治疗必要性。
enSummary: Check jurisdiction, employment, work accident or exposure, causation, and notice; amount and medical necessity may remain disputed.
enTitle: What are the most commonly disputed issues in cases filed at the Commission?
historicAnswer: Some of the main issues in a workers’ compensation case are listed below.  The employee must prove all of them to qualify for benefits. a) Jurisdiction:  on the date of the accident, the employer was subject to the Illinois Workers' Compensation or Occupational Diseases Act. b) Employment:  on the date of the accident, a relationship of employee and employer existed between the parties. c) Accident or exposure:  the employee sustained accidental injuries or was exposed to an occupational disease that arose out of and in the course of employment. d) Causal connection:  the medical condition was caused or aggravated by the alleged accident or exposure. e) Notice:  the employer received notice of the accident or exposure within the time limits set by law. If the employee prevails on these issues, he or she will generally qualify for some benefit, but there may be other issues in dispute.  F or example, the parties may disagree over the extent of the employee’s disability, or the employee’s average weekly wage, or whether the medical treatments and/or bills were reasonable and necessary, or whether the employee is entitled to penalties.

zhSummary: 收集病历与证词，达到最大医疗改善后请求审理；仲裁员依证据作决定。
enSummary: Prepare records and testimony, usually after maximum medical improvement, request trial, and await the arbitrator’s evidence-based decision.
enTitle: How are claims before the Commission resolved?
historicAnswer: An arbitrator of the Commission will conduct a trial, relying on Illinois la w, rules of evidence, precedent set by previous workers’ compensation cases, and the Rules Governing Practice Before the Commission.  A court reporter will make a record of the hearing. Except for emergency hearings, an arbitrator cannot resolve a case until the employee has reached maximum medical improvement.  Once the employee has healed to the extent possible, the parties need to prepare the case for trial by obtaining medical records, doctors’ depositions, and other paperwork.  By the time everything is ready for trial, it is not uncommon for one to two years to have elapsed since the filing of the claim with the Commission. In order to proceed to a trial, a trial date must be requested at the arbitrator’s status call.  The schedules for arbitrator status calls are available at the Commission’s website at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/calendars.htm.  After the trial, the arbitrator will issue a decision within 60 days, stating the amount of benefits, if any, to which the employee is entitled. 10

zhSummary: 19(b) 与 19(b-1) 是不同的加速程序，只先处理指定争点，永久失能等事项仍可能留待后续。
enSummary: Sections 19(b) and 19(b-1) offer different expedited paths for specified issues; remaining issues return to the ordinary case.
enTitle: Is there a way to get a quicker decision if there is an emergency?
historicAnswer: Yes. There are two methods of obtaining an emergency decision.  They are commonly referred to 19(b) hearings and 19(b-1) hearings. For both 19(b) and 19(b-1) hearings, once the issues contained in the emergency process are decided, the case will go back on the arbitration call to resolve other issues in dispute, such as the degree of permanent disability. 19(b) Hearings Under Section 19(b) of the Workers’ Compensation Act, the Commission is required to issue a decision within 180 days of the date the Petition for Review was filed. An employee who claims to be owed medical or compensation benefits may file a 19(b) petition, regardless of whether the employee is working. An employer that is paying TTD may also file a 19(b) petition, as long as it keeps paying TTD until: a) the arbitrator rules on the petition; b) the employee’s medical provider releases him or her back to regular work; or c) the employee starts work of any kind. Neither the employee nor the employer is entitled to a 19(b) hearing if the employee has returned to work and the only benefit in dispute amounts to less than 12 weeks of TTD. 19(b-1) Hearings Under Section 19(b-1), the Commission is required to issue a decision within 180 days, but it should be noted that there are many technical requirements to this process. An employee who claims to be unable to work as the result of an injury and who is not receiving medical benefits or TTD may file a 19(b-1) petition to obtain a quick ruling on the medical care and/or TTD issues.

zhSummary: 员工或雇主可请求由三名委员组成的小组复核记录和书面论点。
enSummary: Either side may seek review by a three-commissioner panel using the hearing record and arguments.
enTitle: Is it possible to appeal the arbitrator’s decision?
historicAnswer: Yes.  The employee and the employer each have the right to appeal a decision.  A panel of three commissioners (usually called the Commission) will review the arbitrator’s decision, as well as the evidence and transcript of the trial.  Both sides may submit written arguments to the Commission. The Commission will then conduct a hearing (called an oral argument) at which the parties may present a brief, 5-10 minute argument for their position.  The Commission is required to issue its decision within 60 days.

zhTitle: 上诉期间是否马上付款
zhSummary: 手册说明上诉期间仲裁裁决的款项未必立即支付；最终结果可能附带利息。
enSummary: Payment of an arbitrator’s award may await appeal; interest can be added depending on the final result.
enTitle: Does the employer have to pay the award for benefits while the appeal is pending?
historicAnswer: While an appeal is pending, the employer is not required to pay the benefits awarded by the arbitrator.  If the case is ultimately resolved completely in the employee’s favor, interest will be added to the award, based on governmental bond rates at the time of the decision.  There is also a 1% per month interest charge on medical bills, payable to the medical provider.

zhTitle: 委员会裁决后还能上诉吗
zhSummary: 多数案件可进入巡回法院并可能继续上诉；州政府员工案件有特别终局规则。
enSummary: Many Commission decisions can be reviewed in circuit court and beyond; state employee cases have a special finality rule.
enTitle: Is there any way to appeal the Commission’s decision?
historicAnswer: Commission decisions are final for cases involving employees of the State of Illinois.  In all other cases and for cases involving Workers’ Compensation Commission employees, either party may appeal to the circuit court, which may result in further appeals to the Appellate Court, and in some cases, to the Illinois Supreme Court.  A chart at the end of this section illustrates the process. 11

zhSummary: 双方以协议金额解决争议，须理解放弃的内容，而非只看眼前付款。
enSummary: A settlement exchanges agreed compensation for resolution of the claim; understand exactly which future rights it closes.
enTitle: Is there any other way to resolve disputes?
historicAnswer: As in other court systems, most cases filed at the Commission are resolved through a compromise settlement between the parties.  For cases at the Commission, these arrangements are referred to as “settlement contracts.”  A settlement contract is an agreement between the employee and the employer to close a claim in exchange for an agreed-upon amount of money.

zhSummary: 双方用确定金额换取较快结案，并接受可能高于或低于审理结果的风险。
enSummary: Settlement trades the uncertainty of trial for an agreed result, often with a faster resolution.
enTitle: Why do employers and employees enter into settlement contracts?
historicAnswer: By settling a case, the employee avoids the risk of either getting no compensation or less than is provided in the settlement, and the employer avoids the risk of paying more.  Usually, cases are resolved faster by settlement than by trial.  On average, a settlement is approved approximately two years after a claim is filed.

zhSummary: 使用 IWCC 和解合同并取得批准；自行代理者有额外的当面审查要求。
enSummary: The parties use an IWCC settlement contract and obtain approval; self-represented claimants face additional review.
enTitle: How do employers and employees enter into settlement contracts?
historicAnswer: If the employer and employee reach an agreement, they should write down the terms of their agreement on the Commission’s Settlement Contract form and present it for approval to the arbitrator assigned to the case.  A settlement is not legally binding unless the Commission approves it. An employee who does not have an attorney (called a “pro se” petitioner) must appear in person before the arbitrator who, before approving it, will review the settlement and make sure it is fair and that the employee understands its effect.  Please n ote that the arbitrator will act as a neutral adjudicator, not as the employee’s advocate.

zhSummary: 核对未来现金和医疗福利是否被终结；如需保留，必须在合同中明写。
enSummary: Check whether future cash and medical benefits end; any benefit kept open must be written into the contract.
enTitle: Are there any consequences to a settlement contract?
historicAnswer: It is important for all parties to review a settlement contract carefully.  An approved settlement contract generally terminates the employee’s rights to any future cash or medical benefits, even if his or her condition worsens.  If the parties want to keep a benefit open, this should be clearly stated in the settlement contract.

zhSummary: 未经委员会批准通常不能最终关闭员工权利；事故后极早达成的和解有特别审查风险。
enSummary: An unapproved settlement generally does not close rights; very early settlements receive special scrutiny.
enTitle: Can a settlement be made without the Commission’s approval?
historicAnswer: A settlement that is made without Commission approval does not close out the employee's rights, and the time in which an employee may file a claim with the Commission is extended indefinitely. Any settlement contract made within seven days of the injury is presumed to be fraudulent.

zhSummary: 一次性付款方便但可能结束其他权利；应检查合同范围。
enSummary: A lump sum can simplify payment but may extinguish other rights; read the exact terms.
enTitle: What is a lump sum settlement?
historicAnswer: The Workers’ Compensation Act also allows for settlements that pay an injured employee in a single payment.  Lump sum settlements may end other rights.  It is important to read any settlement carefully and consult an attorney for legal advice.

zhSummary: 和解通常最终关闭案件；裁决后某些医疗请求或残疾程度变化仍有特定申请窗口。
enSummary: A settlement usually closes the case, while some post-award medical or disability changes have limited petition windows.
enTitle: Does a decision or settlement close a case forever?
historicAnswer: A settlement contract usually closes a case forever unless the parties specifically state otherwise in the terms of the settlement contract.  The following changes may occur after a decision or settlement is approved: a) At any time after a decision, the employee may request additional medical services that are reasonably required to cure or relieve the effects of the injury or disease.  If the employer does 12 not agree to the request, the employee may file a petition asking the Commission to resolve the dispute. b) Within 30 months after the Commission issues a decision or approves a settlement contract payable in installments, if an employer can show that the disability has decreased, it may file a petition for a reduction in benefits.  Conversely, if an employee can show that the disability has increased, he or she may file a petition for additional benefits. c) Within 30-60 months after the Commission issues a decision or approves a settlement contract payable in installments for wage differential benefits, if an employer can show that the disability has decreased, it may file a petition for a reduction in benefits.  Conversely, if an employee can show that the disability has increased, he or she may file a petition for an increase in benefits. d) Anytime after the Commission issues a decision for permanent total disability, if the employer can show that the employee is no longer totally disabled, the employer may p etition the Commission for an order terminating the PTD payments.

zhSummary: 可依情形向巡回法院申请执行，或向 IWCC 请求迟延付款罚款与律师费。
enSummary: Possible remedies include circuit-court enforcement and Commission petitions for penalties or fees, depending on the facts.
enTitle: What if the Commission awards benefits, but the employer won't pay?
historicAnswer: The employee may take one or more of the following actions: a) file a petition in the circuit court, asking the court to order payment under Section 19(g) of the Act; b) file a petition with the Commission for penalties and/or attorneys’ fees for delay in payment, as appropriate, under Sections 16, 19(k), and/or 19(l) of the Act; c) file a petition with the Commission alleging a policy of delay or unfairness by the insurer or self- insurer under Section 4(c) of the Act; or d) call the Consumer Services Division of the Illinois Department of Insurance (toll-free 866/445- 5364 or 217/782-4515).

zhSummary: 案件通知会列明状态听证地点；上诉口头辩论有不同安排，应看现行日历。
enSummary: The case notice identifies its hearing site; appeal arguments follow a separate schedule, so check the current calendar.
enTitle: Where are hearings held?
historicAnswer: Arbitrators hold hearings at numerous sites around Illinois.  The employee and named employer on a claim will receive a notice from the Commission indicating the hearing site where the status hearings for the case are to be held. For cases that have been appealed to the Commission after a deci sion has been entered by an arbitrator, the commissioners hold oral arguments in Springfield and Chicago. For a complete schedule and list of hearing sites, please visit the Commission’s website at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/calendars.htm.

zhSummary: 合理必要的治疗可包含急诊、手术、复健、药物、器具，特定情况下也可能涉及住宅改造。
enSummary: Reasonably necessary care can include emergency services, surgery, therapy, drugs, devices, and sometimes home modification.
enTitle: What medical benefits are covered under the Act for work-related injuries?
historicAnswer: The employer is required to pay for all medical care that is reasonably necessary to cure or relieve the employee from the effects of the injury.  This includes, but is not limited to first aid, emergency care, doctor visits, hospital care, surgery, physical therapy, chiropractic treatment, pharmaceuticals, prosthetic devices, and prescribed medical appliances. The cost of devices, such as a shoe lift or a wheelchair, may be covered.  If the work injuries result in a disability that requires physical modifications to the employee’s home, such as a wheelchair ramp, the employer may have to pay those costs as well.

zhSummary: 未被争议的工伤医疗费通常由雇主直接付给医疗机构；共付额与免赔额规则需看具体承保安排。
enSummary: The employer generally pays undisputed work-injury bills directly to providers; copay and deductible treatment depends on coverage.
enTitle: Who pays for the medical care?
historicAnswer: If the employer does not dispute a medical bill, it will pay the medical provider directly.  The employee is not required to pay co-payments or deductibles, unless the service is covered under a group health plan

zhSummary: 案件待审且机构获知 IWCC 申请后，余额催收受限制；员工仍应及时提供案件编号等信息。
enSummary: Balance collection is restricted during a pending case after notice to the provider, but the worker must supply requested case information.
enTitle: Can a doctor send the employee a bill for the medical care for a work-related injury while a case is pending at the Commission?
historicAnswer: While a case is pending at the Commission, the provider cannot try to collect payment from the employee once the employee notifies the provider that he or she has filed a claim with the Commission to resolve this dispute.  This is a practice known as “balance billing.” The provider may send the employee reminders of the outstanding bill, and ask f or information about the case such as the case number and status of case.  If the employee does not provide the information within 90 days of the date of the reminder, the provider may resume its efforts to collect payment.

zhSummary: 通常可选择医生，但 PPP 网络与“两条转诊链”规则会影响选择；急诊和急救通常不计入两次选择。
enSummary: Choice is usually allowed within PPP or two-provider rules; emergency care and referrals have special treatment.
enTitle: Can the employee choose a doctor or hospital from which to receive treatment?
historicAnswer: Generally, the employee may choose the provider where he or she seeks treatment.  However, there may be some limitations both on the number of providers seen by the employee or on which particular providers that an employee may choose.  The employee must choose carefully so that he or she does not end up becoming personally responsible for medical bills. The employee’s choice of provider will be limited to a selected network of providers if an employer has established what is called a Preferred Provider Program or “PPP .”  If there is a PPP, the employee has a choice of two physicians from the network within the PPP. If an employer does not have a PPP, then the employee has a choice of any two providers.  This does not include referrals from those two providers.  First aid and emergency care are not considered to be one of the employee’s two choices.  Nonemergency care obtained before the employee reports the injury to the employer does not count as one of the two choices.

zhSummary: 雇主若使用首选医疗提供者计划，应以规定的书面通知告知员工。
enSummary: An employer using a Preferred Provider Program must give the prescribed written notice.
enTitle: How will an employee know if their employer has a PPP?
historicAnswer: If an employer has established a PPP, it must inform the employee about the PPP in writing on a form that is promulgated by the Commission. 15

zhSummary: 员工可书面退出；退出会计作一次医疗机构选择，之后的选择仍受限制。
enSummary: A worker may decline the PPP in writing, which counts as one provider choice; later choices remain limited.
enTitle: Is an employee only allowed to choose providers from the PPP network?
historicAnswer: The employee may decline participation in the PPP at any time by sending the employer a written statement.  If the employee declines participa tion, it counts as one of the two choices of medical providers. If the employee declines participation in the PPP, the employee may choose any doctor or hospital, and go to any doctor to whom the employee is referred by that provider.  If the employee w ishes to see another chain of providers, however, the employer must approve.

zhTitle: 网络医疗不合适怎么办
zhSummary: 如 PPP 或第二选择提供不当或不足的治疗，可向 IWCC 申请解决。
enSummary: Petition the Commission if PPP care or the second provider’s care is improper or inadequate.
enTitle: What if the employee believes the PPP or the second choice of provider is providing improper or inadequate medical care?
historicAnswer: In this situation, the employee may petition the Commission.  If the Commission finds the provider’s care is improper or inadequate, the employee may choose a provider at the employer’s expense.

zhSummary: 到 IWCC 现行表格页面取得，不使用旧手册的网址。
enSummary: Get the current PPP notice form from the IWCC forms page, not the old handbook URL.
enTitle: Where can employers obtain the form informing employees about its PPP?
historicAnswer: This form is available on the Commission’s website at http://www.iwcc.il.gov/forms.htm .

zhTitle: 选对医生就保证报销吗
zhSummary: 不是；治疗仍须合理必要，利用审查结果会与其他证据一并评估。
enSummary: No. Care still must be reasonably necessary; utilization review is weighed with other evidence.
enTitle: As long as the employee stays within the limits on their choice of provider, will the employer then pay for all medical care?
historicAnswer: Employers may use other methods under the Workers’ Compensation Act to evaluate or challenge the necessity of medical care sought by an injured employee. An employer may perform what is called a “utilization review,” which is a review of the employee’s past, present, and f uture medical treatments related to the work injury, and analyze the necessity of those treatments.  The Commission will consider the utilization review finding, along with all other evidence, when determining whether a treatment was reasonably necessary. If the Commission finds that a medical treatment was not reasonably necessary, the employer will not be responsible for paying the bill.  The employee is not responsible for any treatment the Commission finds to be excessive or unnecessary.  The employe e may be held responsible for treatment that is deemed not covered under the Act.

zhSummary: 及时就医、配合合理治疗、告知工伤性质、提供医疗机构资料及与案件相关的记录。
enSummary: Seek care promptly, cooperate with reasonable treatment, identify the work connection, and supply relevant provider and medical information.
enTitle: What are the employee’s responsibilities regarding medical care?
historicAnswer: The employee should take the following steps in terms of medical care: a) Seek first aid or medical attention immediately after the injury or the point at which gradual symptoms first begin affecting physical activities at work or at home. b) Cooperate with the doctors and make efforts to achieve a complete recovery and full return to work, if possible.  An employee may lose their eligibility for benefits for injurious or unsanitary activities. c) Tell the medical providers that the treatment is for a work -related condition.  This lets the providers know that the employer is responsible for the medical bill. d) Give the employer the name and address of the doctor or hospital chosen.  If the employee changes providers, the employee should again notify the employer. The employee must also give the employer enough medical information for the employe r to determine whether to accept or deny the claim.  This includes all medical records relevant to the condition for which benefits are sought.  An employee is not required to give anyone free access to his or her doctor or medical records, however. 16 The employer is not required to provide benefits if it does not receive the medical information necessary to determine the employee’s medical status and fitness to work.

zhSummary: 在书面协议及法定体检条件满足时，可依被认可宗教的方式接受精神治疗。
enSummary: With a written agreement and required examinations, religious spiritual treatment may be recognized under the Act.
enTitle: What if an injured employee has religious beliefs that prevent him or her from seeking medical treatment?
historicAnswer: If an employee and employer agree in writing, and if the employee submits to all physical examinations required by the Act, the employee may, in good faith, rely on treatment by prayer or spiritual means alone in accordance with the tenets and practice of a recognized church or religious denomination.  An injured employee who denies treatment in accordance with this provision will not suffer any loss or reduction of workers’ compensation benefits.

zhTitle: 必须接受雇主的个案经理吗
zhSummary: 员工可拒绝或限制雇主聘用的个案经理；仍须提供与索赔相关的医疗记录。
enSummary: A worker may decline employer-hired case management without penalty, while supplying relevant medical records.
enTitle: Does an employee have to allow employer-hired case managers to manage his or her care?
historicAnswer: No.  An employee may, without penalty, refuse or limit the involvement of nurses or case managers hired by the employer.  The employee is obligated to provide medical records that are relevant to the case, but otherwise an employee’s medical care is confidential. While case management is not mandatory, an employee may find the assistance of case management helpful.

zhTitle: 雇主可安排独立体检吗
zhSummary: 可以，但须合理通知与安排，并补偿因体检产生的工资损失和合理交通餐费。
enSummary: The employer may request its own medical exam with reasonable notice and location, reimbursing specified lost wages and expenses.
enTitle: Can the employer ask for an evaluation of an employee by its own doctor?
historicAnswer: Yes.  The employer may order a full medical exam by the doctor of its choice.  The employer must provide notice of the exam to the employee and the exam must be at a time and place reasonably convenient for the employee.  If submitting to the examination causes the employee loss of wages, the employer must provide reimbursement for the wages and also the expense of travel and meals.

zhSummary: 雇主医生应向双方提供报告，至少在仲裁听证前 48 小时交付。
enSummary: The employer’s examiner must provide the report to both sides, at least 48 hours before arbitration.
enTitle: Can the employee review the examiner’s report?
historicAnswer: The employer’s doctor must give both parties the examiner’s report as soon as practicable, but not less than 48 hours before an arbitration hearing.

zhSummary: 多数服务受医疗费表约束，通常按实际收费与费表额较低者支付；合同费率可能优先。
enSummary: Most care is subject to a fee schedule, generally paying the lesser of the bill or scheduled amount unless a negotiated rate applies.
enTitle: How are prices for medical care determined?
historicAnswer: Most treatments that are covered under the Act and were provided on or after February 1, 2006, are subject to a medical fee schedule.  The employer shall pay the lesser of the provider’s actual charge or the amount set by the fee schedule. If, however, an employer or insurance carrier contracts with a provider for the purpose of providing services under the Act, the rate negotiated in the contract shall prevail. The schedule is posted on the Commission’s website.  Please also refer to the law, rules, Instructions and Guidelines, and the “Medical: Frequently Asked Questions” web page  at www.iwcc.il.gov/faqmed.htm.

zhSummary: 医生认为暂不能工作，或只准轻工作而雇主无法安排时，可能有临时全残福利。
enSummary: TTD can apply when a doctor bars work or authorizes light duty that the employer cannot provide.
enTitle: What are temporary total disability (TTD) benefits?
historicAnswer: TTD is the benefit that an injured employee receives during the period in which the employee is either: (a) temporarily unable to return to any work, as indicated by his or her doctor, or (b) is released to do light-duty work but whose employer is unable to accommodate him or her. 17

zhSummary: 通常持续至返工或达到最大医疗改善 MMI；具体事实可能影响判断。
enSummary: TTD generally continues until return to work or maximum medical improvement (MMI), subject to the case facts.
enTitle: How long can an employee receive TTD benefits?
historicAnswer: The employer pays TTD benefits to an injured employee until the employee has returned to work or has reached maximum medical improvement or “MMI.”

zhSummary: 基础公式是平均周薪 AWW 的三分之二，另受当期最低与最高额度限制。
enSummary: The basic weekly rate is two-thirds of AWW, subject to current minimum and maximum rates.
enTitle: How is the amount of the TTD benefit calculated?
historicAnswer: The TTD benefit is two-thirds (66 2/3%) of the employee’s average w eekly wage, subject to minimum and maximum limits.  The minimums and maximums  for TTD are available in Commission offices and online at www.iwcc.il.gov/benefits.htm.

zhSummary: 通常从受伤前 52 周税前工资入手；兼职、多份工作与短期工作可能改变计算。
enSummary: AWW usually starts with gross earnings in the preceding 52 weeks; multiple jobs or shorter employment complicate it.
enTitle: How is the employee’s average weekly wage (AWW) calculated?
historicAnswer: The calculation of AWW can be complicated and will depend on the facts of each case.  Generally, AWW is based on the employee’s gross (pre-tax) wages during the 52 weeks before the date of injury or exposure.  However, the calculation of AWW may be affected by many different factors, including, but not limited to: if the employee had more than one job at the time of the injury, worked less than 52 weeks, or on a casual basis.

zhSummary: 最初三个失去的工作日通常不付 TTD；若因伤缺勤达到 14 个日历日，则可能补付。
enSummary: The first three lost workdays are generally unpaid unless injury-related absence reaches 14 calendar days.
enTitle: Is there a waiting period for TTD benefits?
historicAnswer: TTD is not paid for the first three lost workdays, unless the employee misses 14 or more calendar days due to the injury.

zhSummary: 手册要求及时启动并按原工资周期付款；停付前应书面解释，迟延可能引发罚款申请。
enSummary: TTD should start promptly and follow the usual pay interval; stopping requires written explanation and unjustified delay may lead to penalties.
enTitle: When is TTD paid?
historicAnswer: The employer should make the first TTD payment within 14 days after receiving notice of the injury. Since delays are common, to facilitate the prompt payment of benefits, we encourage the employee to give the employer a written demand for TTD benefits along with the doctor’s note. If the employer does not pay promptly and cannot justify the delay, the employee may petition the arbitrator to order the employer to pay penalties and/or attorneys’ fees to the employee. The employer should pay TTD at the same interval the employee was paid before the injury (e.g., weekly or biweekly). If an employer stops paying TTD before the employee returns to work, it must give the employee a written explanation no later than the date of the last TTD payment.  If the employer fails to provide this explanation, the employee may petition the arbitrator to assess penalties and/or attorneys’ fees.

zhSummary: 仍在康复、做较低收入的轻工作，直至恢复原工作或达到 MMI。
enSummary: TPD covers reduced earnings during light duty while healing, until regular work resumes or MMI is reached.
enTitle: What are temporary partial disability (TPD) benefits?
historicAnswer: TPD is the benefit that may be received during the period in which an injured employee is still healing and is working light duty, on a part-time or full-time basis, and earning less than he or she would earn in the pre-injury employment.  The employer pays TPD benefits to an injured employee until the employee has returned to his or her regular job or has reached maximum medical improvement. 18

zhSummary: 2011 年 6 月 28 日后受伤，一般以原岗位当前周薪减轻工作税前周薪，再乘三分之二。
enSummary: For post-June 28, 2011 injuries, generally take two-thirds of the gap between current pre-injury-job pay and gross light-duty pay.
enTitle: How is the TPD benefit calculated?
historicAnswer: For injuries that occurred before June 28, 2011, the TPD benefit is two-thirds (66 2/3%) of the difference between the average amount the employee would be able to earn in the pre-injury job(s) and the net amount he or she earns in the light-duty job. For injuries that occurred on or after June 28, 2011, the TPD benefit is two-thirds (66 2/3%) of the difference between the average amount the employee would be able to earn in the pre-injury job(s) and the gross amount he or she earns in the light-duty job. Example: An employee was earning $900/week at the time of injury.  While the employee was off work and recuperating, the pay for the job increased to $925/week.  The employee returns to a light-duty job and earns $500/week. Pre-injury average weekly wage (AWW) = $900 Current AWW of pre-injury job = $925 Post-injury gross pay = $500 Wage differential = $925  –  $500  = $425 TPD  = $425  X  66 2/3%  = $283.33/week The minimums and maximums for TPD are available in Commission offices and on line at www.iwcc.il.gov/benefits.htm.

zhSummary: 手册将这一福利适用于 2006 年 2 月 1 日及之后发生的伤害。
enSummary: The handbook applies TPD to injuries occurring on or after February 1, 2006.
enTitle: Who is eligible for the TPD benefit?
historicAnswer: Individuals whose injuries occurred on or after F ebruary 1, 2006 are eligible to receive TPD benefits.

zhSummary: 可包含求职辅导、监督求职计划、再培训及教育。
enSummary: Vocational rehabilitation can include job-search counseling, supervised search, retraining, and education.
enTitle: What is vocational rehabilitation?
historicAnswer: Vocational rehabilitation includes but is not limited to counseling for job searches, supervising a job search program, and vocational retraining, including education at an accredited learning institution.

zhSummary: 无法回原岗位时，合理必要的康复、培训与附带费用可能由雇主承担；员工也须合理配合。
enSummary: If the worker cannot return to the old job, necessary rehabilitation and training may be covered, with reasonable cooperation required.
enTitle: When is the employee entitled to vocational rehabilitation?
historicAnswer: If the employee cannot return to the pre-injury job, the employer must pay for treatment, instruction, and training necessary for the physical, mental, and vocational rehabilitation of the employee, including all maintenance costs and incidental expenses.  The employee must cooperate in a reasonable rehabilitation program. The employee may choose the provider of such reasonable vocational rehabilitation services or may accept the services of a provider selected by the employer.

zhSummary: 核准康复计划期间可领取生活维持福利，并获支付相关附带费用。
enSummary: An approved rehabilitation program can carry maintenance benefits and incidental expenses.
enTitle: What benefit is the employee entitled to while participating in an approved vocational rehabilitation program?
historicAnswer: An employee is entitled to maintenance benefits, plus costs and expenses incidental to the vocational rehabilitation program. 19

zhSummary: 维持福利不得低于该员工的 TTD 费率。
enSummary: Maintenance benefits cannot be less than the worker’s TTD rate.
enTitle: How is the maintenance benefit calculated?
historicAnswer: The maintenance benefit shall not be less than the employee’s TTD rate.

zhSummary: 手册将资格适用于 2006 年 2 月 1 日及之后发生的伤害。
enSummary: The handbook applies maintenance eligibility to injuries on or after February 1, 2006.
enTitle: Who is eligible for the maintenance benefit?
historicAnswer: Individuals whose injuries occurred on or after February 1, 2006 are eligible for the maintenance benefit.

zhSummary: 达到 MMI 后仍留下永久身体功能损失，但不一定完全不能工作，才进入 PPD 评估。
enSummary: PPD addresses permanent physical loss after MMI, even when the person can still work.
enTitle: What is permanent partial disability (PPD)?
historicAnswer: PPD is: a) the complete or partial loss of a part of the body; or b) the complete or partial loss of use of a part of the body; or c) the partial loss of use of the body as a whole. “Loss of use” is not specifically defined in the law, but it generally means the employee is unable to do things he or she was able to do before the injury. The Commission cannot make a PPD determination until the employee has reached maximum medical improvement or “MMI.”  PPD is paid only if the job -related injury results in some permanent physical loss.

zhSummary: 工资差额、法定身体部位表、整体身体损失、永久容貌损害；同一损失不能重复领取互斥项目。
enSummary: The four paths are wage differential, scheduled body part, person-as-a-whole, and disfigurement, with limits on double recovery.
enTitle: What types of PPD benefits are awarded by the Commission?
historicAnswer: There are four types of PPD benefits: a. Wage differential (Section 8(d)(1) of Workers’ Compensation Act) If, due to the injury, the em ployee obtains a new job that pays less than the pre -injury employment, he or she may be entitled to receive a wage differential  award.  The wage differential award is two-thirds (66 2/3%) of the difference between the amount the employee earns in the new job and the amount he or she would be earning in their prior employment. For injuries that occur before September 1, 2011, benefits shall be paid for the life of the employee.  For injuries that occur on or after September 1, 2011, benefits shall be paid for five years after the date of the award or until the employee reaches age 67, whichever is later. An employee may be compensated for either the loss of wages or the permanent disability related to the same injury, but not both. Example: An employee was earning $1,000/week at the time of injury.  While the employee was off work and recuperating, the pay for the job increased to $1,040/week.  Due to the injury, the employee can only find a job that pays $500/week. Pre-injury average weekly wage (AWW) = $1,000 Current AWW of pre-injury job = $1,040 AWW of post-injury job = $500 Wage differential = $1,040  -  $500  = $540 PPD benefit   = $540  X  66 2/3% = $360/week 20 b. Schedule of injuries (Section 8(e) of Workers’ Compensation Act) The Act sets a value on certain body parts, expressed as a number of weeks of compensation for each part.  (See the chart at the end of this section).  The number of weeks is then multiplied by 60% of the employee’s AWW. If a body part is amputated or if it cannot be used at all, that represents a 100% loss, and the employee is awarded the entire number of weeks listed on the chart.  If the employee sustains a partial loss, the benefit is calculated by multiplying the percentage of loss by the number of weeks listed. Example: An employee earning $500 per week injures his or her thumb, and it is later determined there is a 10% loss of the use of the thumb. PPD weekly rate = $500  X  60% = $300 Number of weeks = 76 weeks  X 10% = 7.6 PPD benefit = 7.6 weeks  X  $300 = $2,280 c. Non-schedule injuries (person as a whole)   (Section 8(d)2) If the condition is not listed on the schedule of injuries, but it imposes certain limitations, the employee may be entitled to a percentage of 500 weeks of benef its, based on the loss of the person as a whole.  The number of weeks is then multiplied times 60% of the employee’s AWW. Example: An employee earning $500/week suffers a back injury that is determined to have caused a 10% loss of the person as a whole. PPD weekly rate = $500  X  60%  = $300 Number of weeks = 500 weeks  X 10%  = 50 weeks PPD benefit = 50 weeks  X  $300  = $15,000 d. Disfigurement (Section 8(c) of Workers’ Compensation Act) An employee who suffers a serious and permanent disfigurement to the head, face, neck, chest above the armpits, arm, hand, or leg below the knee, is entitled to a maximum of 162 weeks of benefits at the PPD rate.  The number of weeks is then multiplied by 60% of the employee’s AWW. A scar must heal for at least six months before a hearing to assess the disfigurement can be held. An employee may not collect compensation for disfigurement and the loss of use for the same body part.  For example, a person who undergoes carpal tunnel surgery and is found to have experienced some loss of use, may be awarded a benefit based on the body part or on the disfigurement from the surgery scars, but not both.

zhSummary: 现行手册列医生损伤报告、职业、年龄、未来赚钱能力、治疗记录等因素，单一因素不应独断。
enSummary: The current handbook lists impairment report, occupation, age, earning capacity, and medical evidence; no single factor alone decides the result.
enTitle: How is the level of disability assessed?
historicAnswer: For injuries occurring before September 1, 2011, the Commission evaluates the physical impairment and the effect of the disability on the injured employee’s life.  Factors that may be considered include the individual's age, skill, occupation, training, inability to engage in certain kinds of activities, pain, stiffness, or limitation of motion. For injuries occurring on or after September 1, 2011, the Commission bases the determination of disability on five factors: 21 (1) an impairment report prepared by a physician using the most current edition of the American Medical Association's “Guides to the Evaluation of Permanent Impairment” (2) the occupation of the injured employee; (3) the age of the employee at the time of the injury; (4) the employee’s future earning capacity; and (5) evidence of disability corroborated by the treating medical records. One of these factors may not be the sole determinant of disability. The relevance and weight of any factors used in addition to the level of impairment as reported by the physician must be explained by the arbitrator in the decision.

zhSummary: 工伤法通常不另付过去的痛苦损失；残余疼痛可作为永久失能的一部分考虑。
enSummary: The Act does not separately pay past pain and suffering; residual pain can factor into permanent disability.
enTitle: Is an employee eligible for compensation for pain and suffering for a work-related injury?
historicAnswer: Employees are not compensated for past pain and suffering, only for the residual pain that is part of the permanent disability.

zhSummary: 部分 PPD 裁决可在法定窗口内请求调整；工资差额和其他类别的窗口不同。
enSummary: Some PPD awards can be modified within statutory windows, which differ for wage differential and other categories.
enTitle: What if the employee’s condition changes?
historicAnswer: For wage differential benefits where the injury occurred on or after February 1, 2006 , if the employee’s physical condition changes during the 60 months after the award becomes final, either party may ask the Commission to adjust the award. For all other PPD categories:  if the employee’s physical condition changes during the 30 months after the award becomes final, either party may ask the Commission to adjust the award.

zhSummary: 可能是两处列明部位完全失用，或永久无法从事存在稳定就业市场的工作。
enSummary: PTD can mean complete loss of two listed body parts or permanent inability to perform work in a reasonably stable labor market.
enTitle: What is permanent total disability (PTD)?
historicAnswer: PTD is either: a) The permanent and complete loss of use of both hands, both arms, both feet, both legs, both eyes, or any two such parts, e.g., one leg and one arm; or b) A complete disability that renders the employee permanently unable to do any kind of work for which there is a reasonably stable employment market.

zhSummary: 每周基本为 AWW 的三分之二，受当期上下限约束，符合条件可长期支付。
enSummary: The basic weekly benefit is two-thirds of AWW, subject to current limits, and may continue for life.
enTitle: What is the PTD benefit?
historicAnswer: A claimant who is found to be permanently and totally disabled is entitled to a weekly benefit equal to two-thirds (66 2/3%) of his or her average weekly wage, subject to minimum and maximum limits, for life. The minimums and maximums for PTD benefits are available in Commission offices and online at www.iwcc.il.gov/benefits.htm.

zhSummary: 若实际或能够重新工作，雇主可申请终止或修改 PTD，不能假定福利绝对不变。
enSummary: If the worker returns or can return to work, the employer may seek modification or termination.
enTitle: Can a PTD recipient ever work?
historicAnswer: If an employee experiences a complete disability that renders the employee permanently unable to do any kind of work, and returns to work or is able to return to work, the employer may petition the Commission to terminate or modify the PTD benefit.

zhSummary: 仲裁裁决的受益人可能从费率调整基金获得法定生活成本调整。
enSummary: An arbitrated award may qualify for cost-of-living payments from the Rate Adjustment Fund.
enTitle: Does the PTD benefit amount stay fixed for life?
historicAnswer: If a case is decided by an arbitrator, an employee will be entitled to cost-of-living adjustments. Beginning on the second July 15th after the award became final, the recipient will receive an cost-of- living payment from the Commission’s Rate Adjustment Fund that reflects the increase in the statewide average weekly wage during the preceding year.  These payments are made monthly.

zhSummary: 符合两套计划条件时可以，但社会保障福利可能因抵扣规则减少。
enSummary: Both may be available if independently eligible, although Social Security can apply an offset.
enTitle: Can an employee receive both PTD and Social Security?
historicAnswer: Yes, if the employee qualifies under the terms of each program.  If an employee receives both benefits, the Social Security Administration will apply a formula that may result in a reduction in the Social Security benefit.

zhSummary: 手册区分历史受伤日期，2006 年 2 月 1 日后致死伤害列为 8,000 美元；核对适用日期。
enSummary: The handbook distinguishes injury dates; it lists $8,000 for fatal injuries after February 1, 2006, subject to date-specific law.
enTitle: What is the burial benefit?
historicAnswer: For injuries resulting in death that occurred before February 1, 2006, a benefit of $4,200 is provided to the survivor or the person paying for the burial.  For injuries resulting in death occurring after February 1, 2006, the benefit is $8,000.

zhSummary: 基础为死者受伤前 52 周税前 AWW 的三分之二，并受当期上下限约束。
enSummary: The basic survivor rate is two-thirds of gross AWW over the 52 weeks before injury, subject to current limits.
enTitle: How is the amount of the survivors’ benefit calculated?
historicAnswer: The benefit is two-thirds (66 2/3%) of the employee’s gross average weekly wage during the 52 weeks before the injury, subject to minimum and maximum limits. 24 The minimums and maximums for the survivors’ benefit are available in Commission offices and online at  www.iwcc.il.gov/benefits.htm.

zhSummary: 配偶及未成年子女优先；没有时再看完全依赖的父母及达到规定依赖程度者。
enSummary: Spouse and children under 18 are primary; dependent parents and others may qualify when no primary beneficiary exists.
enTitle: Who is entitled to the survivors’ benefit?
historicAnswer: The primary beneficiaries of the survivors’ benefit are the spouse and children under the age of 18. If no primary beneficiaries exist, benefits may be paid to totally dependent parents.   If no totally dependent parents exist, benefits may be paid to persons who were at least 50% dependent on the employee at the time of death.

zhSummary: 有合资格子女时福利继续；没有时，配偶可获相当两年福利的最后一次付款。
enSummary: Benefits continue if eligible children remain; otherwise a remarried spouse receives a final lump sum equal to two years of compensation.
enTitle: If the surviving spouse remarries, does this have an effect on eligibility for survivors’ benefits?
historicAnswer: If there are eligible children at the time of remarriage, benefits will continue. If there are no eligible children at the time of remarriage, the spouse is entitled to a final lump sum payment equal to two years of compensation.  All rights to further benefits are extinguished.

zhSummary: 仲裁裁决的遗属福利可能获费率调整基金支付的生活成本调整。
enSummary: Survivors under an arbitrated award may receive Rate Adjustment Fund cost-of-living payments.
enTitle: Does the benefit amount stay fixed for life?
historicAnswer: If a case is decided by an arbitrator, recipients of the survivors’ benefit will be entitled to cost-of- living adjustments.  Beginning on the second July 15th after the award became final, the recipient will receive an amount from the Commission’s Rate Adjustment Fund that reflects the increase in the statewide average weekly wage during the preceding year.  These payments are made monthly.
